articles.title: Ilia Topuria disfruta al volante de un súper exclusivo KTM X-Bow GT-XR de casi 400.000 euros
articles.standfirst: El campeón de la UFC ha pasado unos días en Georgia, donde ha disfrutado de una experiencia de conducción exclusiva en un modelo muy raro de ver
articles.summary: El campeón de la UFC ha pasado unos días en Georgia, donde ha disfrutado de una experiencia de conducción exclusiva en un modelo muy raro de ver
articles.body: Ilia Topuria, además de uno de los mejores luchadores del planeta, es un excelso aficionado a los coches. Y cada vez que tiene ocasión, lo demuestra. La última: al volante de un deportivo súper exclusivo en Georgia. El 'Matador' ha sido visto a los mandos de un deportivo muy raro de encontrar: el KTM X-Bow GT-XR junto al influencer y vendedor de coches de lujo georgiano Saba Mikava. Topuria ha compartido algunas jornadas en Georgia con su amigo, del que ha quedado constancia en redes sociales. Aunque algunos medios le han atribuido a Topuria la posesión del vehículo, en realidad es uno de los múltiples coches que atesora Mikawa en su garaje, ya que en publicaciones anteriores se ha visto al empresario con este mismo vehículo. Eso sí, el doble campeón mundial de la UFC no ha podido resistir la tentación de probarlo, con se ve en el vídeo que ambos han compartido con sus seguidores. El X-Bow GT-XR es el segundo modelo de cuatro ruedas de KTM (después del X-Bow 'a secas' que lanzó en 2008). Deriva de los coches de carreras de la marca austriaca, los X-Bow GTX y GT2 y, a diferencia de su hermano menor, es un vehículo cerrado gracias esa particular carlinga que le asemeja a los aviones de combate. Está impulsado por el conocido propulsor turbo de cinco cilindros y 2.5 litros del grupo Volkswagen, con 500 caballos de potencia. Los transmite, a través de un cambio automático de doble embrague, a las ruedas traseras, por lo que se configura como la máquina perfecta para conductores puristas... como es Ilia Topuria. Su ligereza (apenas 1.325 kilos gracias al empleo masivo de carbono) le permite presumir de prestaciones de infarto: hace el 0-100 en apenas 3,4 segundos y alcanza una velocidad máxima de 280 km/h. De su exclusividad habla bien a las claras su precio, que ronda los 400.000 euros.

articles.title: Aina Bauzá toma la salida de La Ruta del Ron y pone rumbo a la historia
articles.standfirst: Primera mujer española participar en la gran transatlántica que une Saint-Malo (Francia) con Guadalupe, en el Caribe, en solitario, sin escalas ni asistencia
articles.summary: Primera mujer española participar en la gran transatlántica que une Saint-Malo (Francia) con Guadalupe, en el Caribe, en solitario, sin escalas ni asistencia
articles.body: En 2021 le dijo a su jefe que se iba a una regata y volvía en una semana, pero nunca lo hizo. Cinco años después, Aina Bauzá escribe hoy su nombre en la historia del deporte español. La mallorquina, que estudió Ingeniería Náutica y Transporte Marítimo, es la primera mujer de nuestro país en participar en la Ruta del Ron, un reto colosal que se celebra cada cuatro años y que une Saint-Malo (Francia) con Guadalupe, en el Caribe. En total, 3.542 millas náuticas —6.560 kilómetros— en solitario, sin escalas ni asistencia y con el Atlántico como único escenario. Competirá en Class40, la categoría más numerosa y competitiva de la flota. En esta edición, que reúne a 115 patrones -11 de ellos mujeres- Bauzá pone rumbo a la historia. "Es el mayor desafío de mi carrera deportiva", reconocía Bauzá antes de partir. Lo hará con su Class40 Aina B. Ocean Racing – Alice Milliat Foundation, una Fundación que trabaja para mejorar la visibilidad del deporte femenino, reforzar la presencia de las mujeres en todas las profesiones del deporte y promover una práctica deportiva igualitaria y segura. Bauzá dio sus primeros pasos en la vela de niña en el Club de Puerto de Andratx (Mallorca). Tras varios años en la vela olímpica y cuando con 26 ya pensaba que la vela de competición se acababa para ella, descubrió otra manera de navegar: la vela oceánica. Y la aventura la atrapó- "En 2021 un equipo vio mis ganas y me dejó un Mini 6.50 para lo que quedaba de temporada. Así que me quedé. Enganché el barco a la furgoneta y empecé a recorrer Europa. De puerto en puerto. De regata en regata. De astillero en astillero. Vivía en la furgo, dormía muchas veces debajo o al lado del barco, entrenaba cuando había viento, reparaba lo que se rompía y buscaba presupuesto para poder seguir. No era cómodo. No era seguro. No era el camino fácil. Pero era aventura de verdad", recuerda. Y empezó a hacer carrera en Mini 6.50 para después continuar su progresión en Class40 desde Lorient (Francia), epicentro de la vela oceánica. En 2024 estableció un récord al cruzar el Atlántico en solitario desde Cádiz hasta las Bahamas a bordo de un monocasco de 6,50 metros REDO by Ànima Negra. Tardó 30 días, 22 horas y 34 minutos. En 2025 fue seleccionada en la tercera edición de Cap pour Elles con ENGIE, programa que impulsa el acceso de las mujeres a la navegación oceánica profesional. Ese año completó la Transat Café L’Or en Class40 junto a Axelle Pillain y se convirtió en la primera navegante española en terminar esta transatlántica en la categoría. Bauzá comienza hoy su mayor aventura soltando amarras y empezando la navegación en la Ruta del Ron. En esta regata participa también otro español, Pep Costa, de 26 años a bordo del VSF Sports. Nacido en 1999, comenzó a consolidar su carrera internacional con un octavo puesto en la Mini Transat de 2019, antes de competir en el circuito Figaro y dar el salto a Class40. Entre sus resultados se cuentan la victoria en su categoría de la Rolex Fastnet Race 2023 y la tercera posición en Les Sables–Horta 2025. Llega a su debut en la Ruta del Ron como uno de los nombres con aspiraciones de situarse en las posiciones de cabeza de Class40. En total habrá ocho clases: Ocean Fifty (10), Class40 (49), IMOCA (22), Vintage Mono (13) y Vintage Multi (13). Entre los nombres destacados figuran la italoestadeonidense Francesca Clapcich, que llega como líder de las IMOCA Globe Series 2026. Desde su primera edición, en 1978, la Ruta del Ron combina innovación, estrategia y resistencia. La navegación hacia Guadalupe obliga a interpretar sistemas meteorológicos, encadenar maniobras sin relevos y gestionar el descanso con una precisión casi tan decisiva como el rendimiento de la embarcación. Álex Pella, en 2014, ha sido hasta ahora el único ganador español.

articles.title: Fan confidence in the Bears is still high
articles.summary: Fans are feeling good about the Bears, and the Monday night matchup against the Seahawks will show us just how good this team is.
articles.body:
Knocking off the defending AFC champion New England Patriots wasn't enough to sway the 7% of our voters who still lack confidence in the Chicago Bears' direction. This week's Reacts results are pretty much the same as a week ago, when confidence was at 92.7%.

I'm sure we have some visiting voters from the SB Nation sites that cover the Packers, Lions, and Vikings in the poll trying to sway things negatively, but if there are still disgruntled Bears fans out there voting no, I need to know: why?

If a (5-2) record one season after an (11-5) NFC North Championship team that beat the Packers in the Wildcard round and narrowly lost in the Divisional round isn't enough for you to be confident the Bears are heading in the right direction, then what are you waiting for?

Now, to be fair, most of these votes were tallied before the Bears made the all-in move of trading for Jeffery Simmons.

So maybe some of your hesitation in voting yes was that you were waiting for the defensive line to be addressed.

Well, it's been addressed in the biggest way, and the baddest defensive tackle in the NFL now resides in the Windy City.

Simmons goes from the one-win Titans to the high-profile Bears, who have two prime-time games up next, and a bigger media presence can only help his chances at the Defensive Player of the Year Award. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have those odds at +2000, which are the seventh-best.

Simmons is a force multiplier, and the entire defense will benefit from his presence in the middle of the Bears' d-line

Chicago's defense has been generating pressure by blitzing, but Simmons will let them drop more into coverage, which could help their struggling corners.

Nickelback Kyler Gordon is tied for the team lead with 4 sacks in just 2 games, but the Bears may not have to send him off the edge as much with Simmons pushing the pocket.

On Monday night, the Bears play the Seattle Seahawks and one of the best wide receivers in the game, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and when he runs routes out of the slot, Gordon could be counted on to cover.

articles.title: Keys to the Game: How Titans Can Tame Bengals on the Road
articles.summary: Facing a post-trade defensive void, Tennessee must pressure Joe Burrow and unleash Tony Pollard to spark a monumental upset against the high-flying Bengals a...
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans have a tough road matchup in their first game since the Jeffery Simmons trade.

They have to face the Cincinnati Bengals on the road at Paycor Stadium in Week 8. Joe Burrow and the Bengals are 4-2 after a comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens last weekend.

The Titans are 1-6 after blowing a 14-0 first-quarter lead to the Cleveland Browns . The Browns beat the Titans in a heartbreaker, 27-24, after a game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt.

The Titans were able to get their first win of the year on the road back in Week 6, but the Bengals are a much better team than the Indianapolis Colts.

It's going to be hard to pull off the upset without Simmons on the Titans' sideline. Here are my three keys to a road win for Tennessee:

The Bengals have just two losses this season.

The one similarity in these two losses is that the Bengals turned the ball over. Burrow threw two interceptions in the 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, and the Pittsburgh Steelers recovered two fumbles in their 30-27 win over the Bengals earlier in the year.

One way that the Titans can help themselves out with this is by putting pressure on Burrow.

Losing Simmons was a big blow to the defense; there's no denying that.

Unlike last year, the Titans still have players who can get after the quarterback. Jacob Martin and Jermaine Johnson each have over three sacks this season.

Whether Robert Saleh has to get creative with his blitz packages or not, if the Titans can win the turnover battle, they can win the game.

Tony Pollard had an awesome game against the Browns.

He helped keep the Titans' offense moving, even in the fourth quarter when they were in search of a late touchdown. The Titans prioritized establishing the running game, and it paid off, even if they didn't leave with a win.

The things you have to do on the road to expect a win are run the football well and bring your defense.

Getting Pollard his touches should be priority No. 1 for the Titans, especially with Carnell Tate out for the game.

It's going to be tough to pass the football without Tate. The running game can help with that.

Another thing that the Bengals doing very well is convert on third downs.

They lead the league in conversion rate, first downs per pass, quarterback accuracy and touchdown rate on third down.

The Titans do not need to do the Bengals any favors by letting them get in manageable third-down situations. Keeping Burrow and the offense backed up on third down is a good recipe for success.

If the Titans do these three things, they'll have a good shot at a road win against the Bengals. Kickoff is set for noon CT on CBS.

articles.title: Pirates Should Go After All-Star Reliever to Bolster 2027 Bullpen
articles.summary: The Pirates need to make some big moves this offseason.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates were able to put together a nice 2026 season, even with the team failing to qualify for the postseason.

Pittsburgh ended the year with a record of 82-80 for the season, falling short of breaking the long postseason drought. But even with this, there is a lot to be excited about for the Pirates going forward.

This team has a nice collection of young talent on the roster, and multiple players seemed to take steps forward in development this past season. Pittsburgh will now be entering the offseason looking to add to the team, but how the front office decides to go about this could determine everything for 2027.

With the improvement that the Pirates had this past season, the front office has to spend some money this offseason. If they go against the grain to spend even a little, it could give the roster enough firepower to go after a postseason spot next year.

One area that could be improved is the bullpen , and this could help out the team in multiple different ways. Pittsburgh has a good core of starting pitchers, but the bullpen could use some work this winter.

As the Pirates search for ways to improve the relievers, one name that could make a lot of sense is veteran left-hander Adrian Morejon. Morejon has spent his career with the San Diego Padres so far, and he is now hitting free agency, with multiple teams expected to go after him.

The Padres will likely try to retain him, but the Pirates should look to try to poach him this offseason. The left-hander has put together multiple strong seasons for the Padres over the years, with him being a key relief option in late-game situations.

Last season, Morejon posted a 2.83 ERA over 76 appearances for the Padres, while striking out 107 batters over 86.0 innings of work. The left-hander also was able to save three games for San Diego, and he was one of the more trusted guys in a dominant bullpen.

While Morejon could cost the Padres to open the checkbook a little bit, he could be just what this team needs. Pittsburgh has a closer for next season, with lefty Mason Montgomery emerging this year, but Morejon could give them a nice one-two punch.

Teams that have strong bullpen units tend to do well come playoff time, and the Pirates should try to emulate other staffs. Spending money on Morejon could be a risk, like any signing, but his continued dominance on the mound could offer some relief.

Overall, this could be a good move for the Pirates to consider, even if it may be unlikely due to the price tag. But Morejon could be the splash signing that Pittsburgh has been waiting for.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers' Trade Deadline Plans Receive Speculation After Huge Trade
articles.summary: After reuniting with All-Pro DeForest Buckner, San Francisco may bypass further high-profile deals as key offensive weapons return from injury to solidify a...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers made a real upgrade on the defensive side. After an offseason of clamor over how the team would bolster its pass rush, the Niners traded for former San Francisco defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.

The 49ers are doing well enough they could reasonably have decided to roll with the team they have into the stretch run of the season. After making the big addition, some suggest they may be done making big moves.

San Francisco 49ers on SI's Niles Hall made the case for why San Francisco might be done making big trades before the deadline. Here's what Hall had to say on the potential that Buckner may be all the Niners do in the way of significant moves before the deadline on November 11.

"The 49ers went all in, trading a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for two-time All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

Fans and media have speculated that the 49ers will continue this aggressiveness and attempt to trade for New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson or Los Angeles Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack; yes, these players are game changers, but the 49ers can find answers within.

The 49ers' biggest concern is at wide receiver after a fast offensive start to the season stalled in the last couple of weeks due to injuries at the position.

Last week against the Atlanta Falcons, the wide receiver struggles boiled over, and a 49ers wide receiver didn't have a single catch until the second half. The Niners were without Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson.

On Tuesday, head coach Kyle Shanahan said the three wide receivers will have a chance to return after the bye week, making it unnecessary to trade for Wilson, especially with recent developments from receiver Jordan Watkins. The 49ers will also get back first-round pick De'Zhaun Stribling, who will return at the end of the season."

San Francisco could trade for a receiver. Then again, haven't they already tried adding receivers?

The Niners went out and signed Mike Evans, Christian Kirk and Deebo Samuel in addition to drafting De'Zhaun Stribling. So, they could go and add another player, but if he gets hurt as well, you're still back to square one. Obviously, that's a narrow way of thinking, but that's not to say the Niners are above taking that thought process.

San Francisco is a contender, but they could become an even bigger threat to a Super Bowl run with each addition. We'll monitor whether or not the Niners feel that adding an elite defensive lineman in Buckner is enough to secure a playoff run.

articles.title: Avary Cain’s development could lift Oregon women's basketball season
articles.summary: Oregon women's basketball's offseason was focused more on development than adding new pieces. No one is more key to that strategy than Avary Cain.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks and coach Kelly Graves bet on themselves heading into a pivotal 2026-27 women's basketball campaign .

Fresh off back-to-back appearances in the second round of the NCAA tournament, the Ducks are hoping their development over the summer while retaining the core of their roster leaps them into the second weekend of the tourney this season.

Though juniors Katie Fiso and Ehis Etute easily return the most production from a year ago, perhaps no one is more representative of that development than guard Avary Cain.

The junior spent one season at UCLA before transferring to Oregon as a sophomore in 2025 and had an up-and-down first season in Eugene. The former five-star prep recruit out of Southern California averaged 3.8 points in 36 games last season, all off the bench in just over 14 minutes per game. But those numbers spiked at various moments throughout the season.

See photos as Oregon women's basketball hosts Bushnell in exhibition

None might have been greater than a 13-point performance in the Big Ten Tournament against Maryland, which included a game-sealing 3-pointer with time winding down.

Heading into her third collegiate season and her second at Oregon, Cain has taken on more of a leadership role, as well as a scoring load, as a likely full-time starter.

Graves said in the preseason that Cain has been Oregon's top scorer this summer and fall and it "hasn't been close."

"Something clicked this last spring and she had a great summer and a great fall," Graves said. "She's been a good leader for our young kids, our freshmen. She got here first among our returners and she really kind of led those young kids … it was nice to see her trying to reach out."

The Ducks open their season Nov. 2 at home against Hawaii.

Cain's role will grow even beyond what Graves and the team expected heading into the season. Senior and primary on-ball defender Sofia Bell suffered a season-ending lower body injury in late September, just weeks away from the beginning of the season.

The head of Oregon's defensive attack and one of its captains, Bell's injury is a significant loss for a team returning so much of its rotation.

Enter Cain, who focused the bulk of her first season at Oregon in improving her conditioning and her defensive scout and will likely be tasked with guarding the opposing team's best bigger wings moving forward.

She said she's already taken strides in her on-ball defense and being more engaged on that end as a vocal leader.

"I think that's super important and kind of leading the huddles a little bit more, I'm not really used to that," Cain said of being vocal. "I'm imitating Sofia a little bit ... Defensively, I'm being really tough on myself right now, but I think I'm doing a lot better in that area."

Cain said Graves has been especially tough on her on-ball defense of late, but Graves remarked that she is naturally strong at the top of their base zone defense with good length and size.

"She's got a tough assignment because she's got to take the point but her main responsibility is the high post," Graves said. "She's catting and mousing pretty well, she's got a good feel for it. I think she's got the length and athleticism to be that player defensively, that stopper, she's got to do it consistently. She does it in moments, and she has to do a lot better this year because we need her.

"I'm going to ask a lot of her, but I think she's capable of it."

articles.title: 5 bold predictions for Rams vs. Chargers on Sunday
articles.summary: The Rams could have another big day on the ground against the Chargers in Week 8.
articles.body:
With the Los Angeles Rams taking on a winless Los Angeles Chargers team today , expectations are high. Here are five predictions to accompany such bold thinking.

Williams and Corum go for over 100 yards each

Kyren Williams and Blake Corum went for 99 and 93 yards, respectively, against the Las Vegas Raiders last week. Now against a Chargers team that has yet to display the ability to engineer winning drives, there's no reason for the Rams to attack the air unnecessarily.

It would not be shocking to see them get at least 18 carries each, and with their offensive line and tight ends leading the way, the yardage should be easy to find.

The Chargers' interior offensive line is horrible, and even if they triple-team Aaron Donald, I still don't think they could stop him. Quarterback Justin Herbert always steps up in the pocket, and sometimes he runs into his own linemen. Thus, Donald should be in position to not just record his first sack since returning, but to have two on the day.

Kam Curl has been the undervalued backbone of the Rams' defense, being able to play in a variety of spots, really taking the involvement of the safety to the next level in Chris Shula's scheme. He's a natural safety blanket to prevent the big play, and Herbert has been throwing questionable balls all year.

When the Rams revert to their balanced offense, Matthew Stafford's passing yards may not be as high as they once were, but his efficiency goes through the roof. His ability to read defenses, operate play action, and be comfortable with having his back turned to the defense has been the perfect pairing for their 12 and 13 personnel offenses.

Stafford tosses three scores, while hitting eight different pass catchers on the day. He also has over 22 completions.

With kicker Joshua Karty back in the fold, no one outside of the organization really knows what things will look like with current starter Brandon McManus. Is McManus the kicker, and is Karty doing kickoffs? Is there a certain range that the Rams trust Karty with more?

To spice things up, I predict McManus misses at least one field goal or extra point to make the conversation even more interesting heading into November.

articles.title: Is George Pickens playing today? Cowboys WR start-sit injury update vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Pickens played just 41 snaps in a run-heavy win at Philadelphia, and a new hamstring injury adds more snap-count risk against Arizona.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens is expected to play today against the Arizona Cardinals despite a questionable tag, so fantasy football managers can keep him in Week 8 lineups while watching how many snaps a sore hamstring allows.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning that Pickens is expected to suit up after he was limited in all three practices this week with shoulder and hamstring injuries. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday he expects him to play.

Pickens first landed on the injury report with a shoulder issue Oct. 22, and he played through it in the Oct. 26 win at Philadelphia without a game designation. The hamstring was added this week, and that's what pushed him to a questionable tag for Sunday.

Schottenheimer sounded unconcerned Friday when he said, "I think we're pretty healthy ." Dallas did rule out linebacker Dee Winters and returner KaVontae Turpin, but Pickens, rookie safety Caleb Downs and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams are all expected to play after limited weeks.

Playing time is the bigger fantasy concern. Pickens played 41 snaps at Philadelphia as Dallas ran 38 times for 204 yards, and he still caught four of six targets for 57 yards, including a one-handed, toe-tap touchdown before halftime. If the Cowboys jump out to an early lead, they would likely dial back the passing game early and lean on their running backs.

George Pickens fantasy football outlook vs. Cardinals

The Georgia product has 37 catches for 485 yards and two touchdowns, second on the team behind CeeDee Lamb's 651 yards. He posted at least 73 receiving yards in four straight games before last week's run-heavy script.

Part of the snap dip ties back to blocking. Before the Eagles game, Schottenheimer said Pickens "needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well." Pickens logged 13 run-blocking snaps at Philadelphia, the fewest among Cowboys receivers who played on offense.

The 2-5 Cardinals should push Dallas to throw more than it did against the Eagles, because Jacoby Brissett attempted 48 passes in last week's 30-16 loss to Denver and tight end Trey McBride caught 10 balls for 111 yards. Start Pickens as a WR2 once Dallas confirms he's active roughly 90 minutes before kickoff, with the understanding that the hamstring carries some risk of an early exit.

Should you start Pickens on your fantasy football team? Absolutely. He's a low WR1 against the Cardinals, just outside the top 10 at his position.

Lamb caught five of 12 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns against the Eagles and remains a locked-in WR1. Ryan Flournoy caught all four of his targets for 70 yards in that game, and he'd see more snaps if the hamstring limits Pickens.

Tight end Jake Ferguson went without a catch on his lone target last week, and Luke Schoonmaker had to test a groin injury Friday before Dallas settled its tight end plan.

This is a plus fantasy football matchup for practically all involved. Including Dak Prescott, who threw three touchdown passes at Philadelphia, and the 2-5 Cardinals visit the 3-4 Cowboys at 1 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium.

articles.title: Georgia football reacts to emotional win over Florida
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs took care of it's rival on Halloween day. The Bulldogs react after coming out on top 27-8
articles.body:
After a much needed bye week for the Georgia Bulldogs , they were able to bounce back into the win column as they were able to dominate their rival, the Florida Gators in Atlanta, Georgia at Mercedes Benz Stadium. The Bulldogs came off an upset loss just two weeks ago to the Auburn Tigers at home. Georgia clearly made some adjustments since then and took advantage of their bye week allowing players to get healthy and to fix issues that in large part cost them the game against Auburn . However, the Bulldogs defense looked nothing short of spectacular against the Gators.

The Florida Gators came into this contest playing at a pretty solid level and gave plenty of reason for people to believe they could come into Atlanta and defeat the Bulldogs. The biggest question over the course of this season has been the consistency of quarterback play. Between junior Aaron Philo and redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr. the Gators have had sparks from each signal caller throughout the season. Philo was named the starter prior to the game against the Bulldogs but didn't finish the contest as the starter. Jones Jr. flashed signs but also made some costly mistakes in which Georgia took advantage of.

"I thought Schumann had a good game plan, a very disruptive game plan... the defensive staff did a tremendous job and tried to keep things simple because Buster causes a lot of confusion. We didn't do a whole lot." Smart said.

The Bulldogs defensive staff did an outstanding job against Florida and the biggest highlight of the day for the defense is the fashion they shut down Gators running back Jaden Baugh. Georgia's defense held Baugh to just 38 rushing yards on 17 carries. That was a major performance from the Bulldogs defense and a statement was made on that side of the ball.

Georgia LB Chris Cole reacts to Georgia's win

"We knew coming in that Florida had a lot of good running backs, and especially Baugh, so we had to be able to stop the run and just kind of stop explosive plays." Chris Cole said.

The Bulldogs did exactly that. They stopped the run and slowed down one of the best backs in the SEC this season. Georgia certainly shut down the explosive plays and they were able to contain any short positive plays as well.

The Bulldogs will look to take this momentum on the road next week against another big challenge facing off against the Ole Miss Rebels in Oxford. They will definitely need this kind of defensive play against Ole Miss signal caller, Trinidad Chambliss if they want to come out victorious.

articles.title: 3 things from Charlotte's 109-104 defeat to Philadelphia
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets dropped their third consecutive game Saturday night, falling to the Philadelphia 76ers 109-104.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets dropped their third consecutive game Saturday night, losing to the Philadelphia 76ers , who improved to 6-1 without two of their starters, LeBron James and Joel Embiid. Despite leading for 67% of the game, Charlotte couldn't hold on in the fourth, as they were outscored 32-21 in the final frame on their home floor, leading to a 109-104 defeat. Prior to the Hornets' next matchup against the Detroit Pistons , here are three things to take note of.

3. Tidjane Salaun appears ready for more minutes

In the absence of Kon Knueppel, Sion James has been Charlotte's starting shooting guard, with Dennis Schroder being the natural Coby White replacement at point guard. Although James had an impressive preseason, the former Duke guard has struggled immensely to begin his sophomore season, shooting 18.9% from the field and 15.6% from 3-point range. That continued Saturday, as James finished with a plus-minus of -21, the lowest on the team. All the while, Tidjane Salaun has stood out in the second unit, finding confidence in his long range shooting and his defense. Salaun is shooting 38.5% from 3-point range and a career-best 55% from the field. However, the Frenchman is averaging a career-low 13.8 minutes per game.

2. Increased energy on the second-night of a back-to-back

The Hornets came out with a different energy Saturday night, after a 79-point performance against the Wizards Friday night. This has been a familiar trend for Charlotte to begin the year, as they excelled on the second night of a back-to-back against the Miami Heat, after being blown out by the Atlanta Hawks a day prior. While the Hornets didn't get the win Saturday like they did against the Heat, Hornets fans should be happy with the team's effort on short rest against Philadelphia.

1. Charlotte's need for scoring couldn't be more apparent

Although Grayson Allen was phenomenal for the Hornets Saturday night, a 27-point effort on 9-for-12 shooting is difficult to expect every night. Brandon Miller added 24 points, as the two nearly combined for half of the team's 104 points on their own. Early on, it's not surprising that Charlotte ranks dead last in offensive rating to start the year. While this will change upon the return of White and Knueppel, role players like Schroder, Allen and Naz Reid need to create consistent offense in the meantime.

The Dodgers have three months to prepare for spring training 2027, while also figuring out what they need to do before the impending lockout begins.

Nine players from the 2026 team have now reached free agency, and Tarik Skubal is the prized possession that every team will have their eyes on this offseason. Even with Skubal's indefinite future with the team, the Dodgers still possess one of the strongest teams not just in the National League, but in all of baseball. The triumvirate of MVPs at the top of the lineup remains a constant, and the team still has a four-headed monster in the rotation once Shohei Ohtani returns to his two-way status.

Sonja Chen of MLB.com analyzes how the Dodgers may shape up for the 2027 season— regardless of Skubal's landing spot— signifying a potential youth movement that can help energize an aging core.

The Dodgers never shy away from bringing in free agents or swinging trades, but they should be able to upgrade some areas of their roster internally. Let's take a stab at making a way-too-early Opening Day roster projection, exclusively with players who are already in the organization.

Stephen J. Nesbitt, Chad Jennings and Tim Britton of The Athletic have already created a way-too-early power rankings for the 2027 season. The obvious top spot goes to the now-reigning World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, but the Dodgers are right behind them at the no. 2 spot.

The point is, even after their flaws were exposed in the National League Championship Series, these are still the Dodgers. Fourteen straight playoff appearances. Three championships in the past seven years. Five pennants in the past 10. So, yeah, whatever the new collective bargaining agreement brings, we're guessing they'll find a way to be pretty good next year, too.

The Dodgers are no strangers to having an exorbitant offseason, as they have shown over the last three years. The team will once again be frontrunners for high-end talent, but they might also be in the market to either acquire or send away start talent, notes Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times .

If the solution involves personnel changes, however, a trade might be necessary to shake up the Dodgers' veteran position-player group. Whether the Dodgers would want to part with one of their clubhouse leaders, and whether another team would be interested in taking on (or the Dodgers would pay down) any of those contracts, remains to be seen.

articles.title: Today in White Sox History: November 1
articles.summary: Mark Buehrle’s glove is golden, once again
articles.body:
1946 Future White Sox owner (and current Cleveland owner) Bill Veeck has his right foot amputated. Veeck had suffered a grievous injury to his leg while serving in the South Pacific in World War II, and complications from that injury resulted in this dramatic development. True to his nature, however, Veeck eventually made his loss of leg (soon enough, he would lose his entire right leg, up to his knee) its own celebration of sorts, as he chose a pirate's peg-leg rather than a more proper prosthetic — including a slot for an ashtray in the artificial leg itself!

Veeck had just completed his first partial season as a major-league owner, and he was already innovating; in Cleveland, he bucked tradition by adding National League scores to the list of "other games" on the Municipal Stadium scoreboard.

1950 After 20 years with the franchise, all-time great and career White Sox standout Luke Appling announced his retirement. He was undoubtedly the greatest player in franchise history at the time, and 72 years later comfortably remains the all-time team leader in WAR, with 77.6. He had a career average of .310, with 2,749 hits, won two batting titles, and in 1936 drove in 128 runs.

Upon retirement, Appling took a job managing the Memphis Chickasaws, Chicago's Double-A affiliate. Over three years there, Appling was 247-216, pushing the 87-67 Chicks to a pennant in 1952 and earning minor league manager of the year honors. Appling would later manage in Triple-A and coach at the major-league level for several teams, including the White Sox (1970-71). In his only MLB managing gig, he went 10-30 managing the hapless Kansas City A's in 1967.

1982 The White Sox named Dave Duncan their new pitching coach. The former catcher made a fast name for himself under manager Tony La Russa , but ultimately La Russa's allegiance to Duncan cost both men their jobs, as in 1986 GM Ken Harrelson wanted Duncan dismissed, La Russa refusing.

Together the pair went on to great success in Oakland and St. Louis, and Duncan followed La Russa back to the White Sox in 2021, albeit as a front office pitching consultant, not a coach.

The White Sox traded for Duncan at the end of his career, but when the club cut him in Spring Training 1977 he opted to retire and begin a coaching career.

2011 Mark Buehrle was awarded his third straight Gold Glove — the only player in the American League to repeat the honor from 2010. Sadly, this would be Buerhle's final Gold Glove with the White Sox, as Chicago would let him depart to the Miami Marlins as a free agent five weeks later. Buerhle won a fourth straight Gold Glove in 2012 — the final major award of his career.

2016 A name change went into effect at the ballpark formerly known as U.S. Cellular Field. The Guaranteed Rate mortgage company, based in Chicago, signed a 13-year agreement with the team for naming rights. The ballpark would be called Guaranteed Rate Field.

The announcement was met with a storm of ridicule by many — including the Chicago Bears and Chicago Cubs , who tweeted out negative comments. The company's downward-arrow logo was met with criticism by many White Sox fans, who felt that was not an appropriate connection with a baseball team, particularly one that had been struggling for several seasons.

According to reports, the White Sox asked the company to change the logo on the ballpark sign, but were refused. Rumors also circulated that at least one other company offered more money for naming rights, but insisted on the name changing back to Comiskey Park — which owner Jerry Reinsdorf refused to do.

2018 The White Sox swapped minor league first baseman Justin Yurchak to Los Angeles for Manny Bañuelos . Signed 10 years earlier, at 17, by the Yankees, Bañuelos had spent all but six games of the previous decade working his way though the minors, save for seven games in Atlanta in 2015.

The southpaw pitched poorly in a swingman role after breaking camp with the White Sox in 2019, and then suffered shoulder inflammation in June that effectively sidelined him for the year. Overall, Bañuelos went 3-4 with a 6.93 ERA and -0,4 WAR for the year.

articles.title: How offseason Texas Longhorns moves could make Matas Vokietaitis nation's top center
articles.summary: Texas coach Sean Miller helped reel in power forward David Punch, who will team with Matas Vokietaitis in a loaded frontcourt
articles.body:
Matas Vokietaitis carried a big load for Texas basketball last season.

And that's quite literal, considering the 7-foot, 255-pound center often had to fend for himself in the paint on an undersized Longhorns squad that somehow scrapped its way to the Sweet 16.

But second-year coach Sean Miller says Vokietaitis, a junior from Lithuania, still hasn't tapped his full potential even after averaging 15.6 points and 7.1 rebounds a year ago in his first season at Texas. That's one reason why Miller's program made a heavy investment in power forward David Punch , an All-Big 12 player a year ago at TCU.

Yes, the 6-7, 245-pound Punch provides a knockout on his own after averaging 14.1 points and 6.8 boards last season. But part of his immense value - Punch signed with Texas for a reported $4 million a year - will come from how he helps Vokietaitis, Miller said.

With Punch on the court, Vokietaitis won't face as many double-teams with each touch in the paint. And with a little more freedom for his post on the defense end, Miller said Vokietaitis can work more on his rim protection.

The regular season doesn't start until Monday with a visit from Chicago State, but Vokietaitis already understands the impact Punch has on the team as well as his own development.

"It's like a gift playing with him," Vokietaitis said. "I'm very, very grateful that he's here, and we're ready to be the best frontcourt in the country."

Sean Miller: Matas Vokietaitis plays from love, not just size

That's the expectations for No. 7 Texas , Miller said. Even though almost every young player wants to be the next Steph Curry, the Texas coach knows basketball remains a big man's game. Last year, Vokietaitis was the only Texas player taller than 6-foot-8 to play at least 400 minutes. Now, Vokietaitis, Punch and 6-9 freshman Marcus Spears give Texas the size to match up with the best in the SEC as well as the nation, Miller said.

"I think Marcus' talent, size, athleticism with David and Matas gives us a really unique combination," Miller said. "When you look at the size of that front line, you know that's the size of a lot of teams that you watch that are still playing deep in March."

That's the goal for a Texas team with 11 new faces with five transfers and six freshmen. But Vokietaitis - the lone returning starter from last year's 21-15 squad - remains the key.

When discussing big men, Miller often brings up the myriad conversations he had with the late Bill Walton, a Hall of Fame center who became a much-beloved color analyst for college basketball.

"I love Bill Walton, and he used to talk about there's two types of big guys," Miller said. "One category is a big guy that plays the game of basketball because he's supposed to. He's tall. There's this other guy that he might be tall, but the reason he plays the game is he loves it. And Walton would always ask me, 'Coach, does he play the game because he loves it, or does he play the game because he's supposed to?' And Matas plays the game because he loves it."

Trimming fouls, adding blocks focus for Texas basketball post

Vokietaitis certainly plays with the type of passion that delights his teammates and infuriates the foe. He proved fearless going to the basket a year ago, when he ranked second in the SEC with 7.9 free-throw attempts per game. But he'll also mix it up with opponents, as evident by both the boos from opposing fans as well as foul calls from the officials. That energy caught the attention of freshman guard Austin Goosby the moment he stepped onto the practice court with Vokietaitis.

"Matas, yeah, that's a big dude," Goosby said. "It's great to have a big man that wants to do all the dirty work and go get in the paint and rebound, and he'll still kick it out to you. Just knowing that he has my back and I have his back at the end of the day, we'll be able to do big things. Obviously on the court, you see him, he's probably angry, mad, just trying to take someone's head off. But when he's off the court, he's just a great kid to be around."

But removing heads seems to catch the eye of the officials, and Miller doesn't want that much attention. The coach said trimming the fouls and protecting the rim are two areas of focus for Vokietaitis, who shot 61.9% from the floor and 66.9% from the foul line last season.

"One element that we want him to grow in is just being smarter," Miller said. "He doesn't have to flop, beg for fouls, play that game. He can really just get fouled because he's big and physical and good. And I also think that he has another level that he knows he has to get to defensively. And we've worked really hard this summer to make sure that on an everyday basis that we put him in a position to improve there. So, his defense improving, being smarter, but really picking up where he left off."

David Punch: More than sidekick in frontcourt

And that's where Punch helps. Not only does the graduate of Killeen Harker Heights have a soft jumper that complements Vokietaitis' rugged style, but Punch also plays with a cool demeanor that helps settle down his teammates. He seems to enjoy mixing it up in the paint with players a few inches taller, but playing with a big man like Vokietaitis expands his game. And it expands the Longhorns' options on both ends of the court, Punch said.

"It's super exciting, honestly," Punch said. "I've always kind of been the center, but having Matas has made my game a lot easier. It allows me to step out, kind of worry about the perimeter and not have to worry about being a force on the inside as much. You know, I'm still going to do my stuff around the basket, but Matas just takes a lot of pressure off on defense.

"The last two years (at TCU), I really didn't get to play with somebody like Matas. Playing with him this year, it opens the floor a lot for both of us. I've talked to him, and it's something that we haven't experienced yet, but it's something that we're looking forward to. It's going to be amazing."

Miller thinks so, too. Mixing together a strong offseason with a revamped roster that fits well with his skill set will make Vokietaitis "one of the best centers in college basketball," said the coach.

"Matas has had a great off season," Miller said. "He's a really hard worker, loves the game, and really pours into it what he does. I think he'll pick up where he left off, and I'd be surprised if he didn't.

"He's over 7 feet tall, and he's right at about 5 ½ or 6% body fat," Miller said. "Look, there just aren't a lot of those types of people walking around on planet Earth. It's a testament to his discipline, his work ethic and just his quest to be great."

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu continued her impressive late-season run by clinching the Hylo Open Super 500 title with a commanding straight-game victory over Denmark's Line Hojmark Kjærsfeldt in the final on Sunday.The second-seeded Indian defeated the world No. 25 and eighth seed 21-12, 21-14 in just 39 minutes to claim her second title of the season. The triumph in Saarbrücken, Germany, also earned Sindhu 9,200 ranking points, keeping her in contention for a place at the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals.The 31-year-old had won the Japan Open in July and finished runner-up at the French Open last week. Her victory on Sunday capped another strong week, following her run to the final in Paris, and underlined her consistency as the season approaches its conclusion.Sindhu came into the summit clash with a dominant 6-1 head-to-head record against Kjærsfeldt, whose only previous victory over the Indian had come at the 2025 Sudirman Cup Finals.Sindhu dominates final to secure second titleA former world champion, Sindhu displayed control and precision throughout the final, using her attacking strokes and court coverage to keep the Danish shuttler under pressure.She dictated the exchanges from the outset and opened up a comfortable lead in the first game. Kjærsfeldt struggled to match the Indian's pace and accuracy as Sindhu wrapped up the opening game 21-12.The second game followed a similar pattern. Sindhu maintained her composure, controlled the rallies and prevented her opponent from building any sustained momentum. She eventually converted her advantage into a 21-14 win to seal the title in 39 minutes.Second successive final after French Open runSindhu had entered the Hylo Open final after defeating compatriot Anmol Kharb in straight games in Saturday's semifinal.The Indian registered a 21-13, 21-16 victory over the 19-year-old in 32 minutes to reach her second final in as many weeks. Anmol, ranked world No. 53, was appearing in only her second Super 500 semifinal.Sindhu's experience, attacking game and precise net play proved decisive against the young Indian, who briefly threatened to put pressure on her in both games but could not sustain the challenge.After finishing runner-up in Paris, Sindhu went one step further in Germany. articles.title: Sheila Chepkirui wins matchup of past champions in NYC Marathon, Andreas Almgren makes winning debut
articles.summary: Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men’s race of the New York City Marathon in his debut in the event while Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women’s race for the second time Sunday.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women’s race of the New York City Marathon for the second time in three years on Sunday while Andreas Almgren of Sweden was victorious in his debut in the distance. Chepkirui pulled away from defending champion Hellen Obiri in the final 150 meters to seal the victory in 2 hours, 24 minutes and 36. “The last mile was really tricky,” said Chepkirui, who also won in 2024. “I had to be patient because I knew Hellen was really strong, so I had to really push up to the finish line.” What Chepkirui didn’t know was that American Jessica McClain had been gaining on both of the Kenyans in the final 800 meters of the race. McClain finished 6 seconds behind Chepkirui after passing Obiri — a two-time winner who set the course record in 2025 — in the final few strides. It was the first time a U.S. woman finished in the top three since 2018. “It was a really fun, magical day out there. New York, you never know what to expect and I honestly didn’t feel like amazing through (Mile) 18, and just kind of had to stick in it and adjust as I went,” McClain said. “Top five was top of mind, then podium. I was just like, stick with it. And then all of a sudden Hellen was coming back to me, so I don’t really know what happened, but I couldn’t be happier right now.” Almgren was making his debut at 26.2 miles after a successful career running half-marathons. He pulled away from Yemaneberhan Crippa of Italy in the final mile to take the victory in 2:6.1. “This is my first marathon. I didn’t know how I was supposed to feel,” said Almgren. Crippa finished 13 seconds behind Almgren. Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho was third, edging out defending champion Benson Kipruto. Almgren’s time was the third fastest in the course’s 50-year history, and six runners went under 2:07 to finish in the top 10 all-time times. “I just tried to stay up at front and see what happened and see how the race developed,” Almgren said. “I didn’t think it was going to be that quick of a finish, but I didn’t really know anything about that. One of the reasons I choose to race New York is that you don’t care about the time but just get as good a position as possible.” He became the first marathoner to win his debut in the event since Gebre Gebremariam of Ethiopia won the 2010 race. American Zouhair Talbi finished sixth on Sunday and ran the fastest time ever by a U.S. runner in the event. It was the 50th time that the race has run through all five boroughs of the city. There were just over 2,000 competitors in 1976, the seventh running of the race, including only 88 women. About 60,000 runners stepped up to the starting line Sunday, with nearly half of them women. There were runners from more than 140 countries competing, including defending men’s champion Kipruto. He won in thrilling fashion last year, edging Alexander Mutiso by three-hundredths of a second. The New York City Marathon began in 1970, and the first six years it was run entirely inside Central Park, with runners doing loops. The race was moved out of Central Park in celebration of the U.S. bicentennial and to help uplift the city, which was struggling. It ended up turning into one of the marquee events in New York. Course tweak For the first time in 15 years, there was a minor change in the course. The runners took a slightly different route at Mile 20 when the race entered the Bronx. The move was made to reduce the number of turns in the borough from seven to five and ease some of the street closures in the area. Eight-time winner Marcel Hug won the men’s wheelchair race for the eighth time, edging Daniel Romanchuk by just over a second. Romanchuk made a move to take over the lead in the last mile as the pair entered Central Park for the final time. Hug passed him in the final 100 meters to win. Hug’s Swedish countrymate Catherine Debrunner pulled away from the field early to win the women’s wheelchair race, finishing in 1:40:02. It was the second-fastest time in race history, trailing her own mark by about 30 seconds from 2023. Two-time defending champion Susannah Scaroni finished third, three months after giving birth to her first child, more than eight minutes behind Debrunner.

articles.title: 2026 NYC Marathon: Andreas Almgren wins marathon debut, Sheila Chepkirui captures another win on women's side
articles.summary: Sheila Chepkirui pulled away from last year's winner Hellen Obiri in the final two miles.
articles.body:
In most marathons, you can count on the big names to pull away from the pack. While the 2026 NYC Marathon did see that phenomenon on the women's side, the men's portion of the event featured a surprising first-time winner.

Swedish runner Andreas Almgren won the 2026 NYC Marathon in his marathon debut. While Almgren was an accomplished runner coming into the race — winning medals at the World Championships and other competitions — this was the first time he ran a competitive marathon.

Almgren finished with a time of 2:06:01, beating out last year's winner Benson Kipruto. It took a superhuman 4:30 final mile from Almgren to take the victory.

Kipruto, who won the NYC Marathon in 2025, fell behind in the final stretch. He actually finished fourth, with a time of 2:06:27.

Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa finished second behind Almgren, with a time of 2:06:14. Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho came in third with a 2:06:26 time.

The men's portion of the event featured plenty of lead changes throughout. It took until the final stretch for Almgren to truly emerge as a contender. He ultimately wound up smashing the competition thanks to his incredibly strong finish.

Prior to running the 2026 NYC Marathon, Almgren was an accomplished runner in shorter events. He took home the gold at the World Road Running Championships half marathon in September and the gold in the European Championships 10,000m in August. He set records at both events.

It was quite the marathon debut for Almgren, who now looks like a perennial contender in the sport.

Sheila Chepkirui takes second win at NYC Marathon

Early on, it became apparent that the women's portion of the NYC Marathon would come down to some heavy hitters. That, ultimately, proved to be the case. As the race went on longer, Chepkirui got stronger, pulling away from last year's winner Hellen Obiri and winning the event for the second time in her career.

Things really started to materialize at the halfway point, as it became an eight-person race. A small group — which contained three former winners — broke away from the rest of the pack.

While four American women led the the way around the 15K mark, three Kenyan runners seemed to get stronger as the race progressed. At the 30K mark, Chepkirui of Kenya led the way, but the eight-woman pack were all still in play to win the event.

But with two miles to go, the favorites moved to the front. Chepkirui and Obiri were fighting for that top spot. It was a familiar position for both women, who have combined to win the last three NYC Marathons.

In the end, Chepkirui broke away from Obiri. The Kenyan finished with a time of 2:24:36. It was her second victory at the event, which she last won in 2024.

Surprisingly, Obiri fell behind in the final stages of the race, allowing American Jessica McClain to claim second place. McClain finished with a time of 2:24:42. She barely beat out Obiri, who came in third with a time of 2:24:43.

Marcel Hug wins eighth NYC Marathon, Catherine Debrunner takes second win

In the wheelchair division, Marcel Hug picked up his eighth win. Since 2016, Hug has traded off victories with Daniel Romanchuk. It came down to those two again in 2026, with Hug just barely edging out Romanchuk for the victory. He beat Romanchuk by just 1.13 seconds.

Debrunner, who holds the course record for her win in 2023, picked up her second-ever victory at the event Sunday. She demolished the competition this time around, finishing roughly seven minutes ahead of the field. That wasn't good enough to break her own course record, however, as Debrunner finished 30 seconds off her 2023 time.

articles.title: Sara Guerrero y Cristina Jiménez-Orta, plata y bronce en la Copa de Europa de Ibiza
articles.standfirst: La checa Heidi Juránková se proclamó campeona
articles.summary: La checa Heidi Juránková se proclamó campeona
articles.body: Las españolas Sara Guerrero y Cristina Jiménez-Orta consiguieron este domingo las medallas de plata y bronce, respectivamente, en la Copa de Europa de Triatlón disputada en Santa Eulària des Riu (Ibiza), donde la checa Heidi Juránková se proclamó campeona. La gallega Sara Guerrero completó la prueba en 57 minutos y 45 segundos, a 32 segundos de Juránková, que se impuso con un tiempo de 57:13, mientras que la sevillana Cristina Jiménez-Orta cruzó la meta en tercera posición, con un registro de 57:57. La competición se decidió en el segmento de carrera a pie, después de que las tres primeras clasificadas mantuvieran diferencias mínimas en la natación y el ciclismo, informó la organización. Guerrero fue la más rápida en el agua, con un tiempo de 9:28, seguida de Jiménez-Orta (9:29) y Juránková (9:33), mientras que la checa marcó el mejor registro en bicicleta (30:01). En la carrera a pie, Juránková logró imponerse con un parcial de 16:30, por delante de Guerrero (17:00) y Jiménez-Orta (17:07), lo que le permitió asegurarse la victoria. La actuación española se ha completó con la novena posición de la madrileña Iratxe Arenal, que terminó en 58:33, a un minuto y veinte segundos de la vencedora.

articles.title: Jerry Koosman, one of Mets' greatest pitchers ever, dies at 83
articles.summary: Jerry Koosman, a two-time All-Star and key member of the Mets' 1969 World Series championship team, has died at 83.
articles.body:
Jerry Koosman died, the Mets announced Sunday. He was 83.

One of the greatest pitchers in franchise history, Koosman's No. 36 was retired Aug. 28, 2021, at Citi Field .

"Humbly thankful that they thought that much of me to retire my number," he said before his ceremony five years ago . "I know I'm joining a great crew that's already had their numbers retired. I don't know that I deserve it, but I guess we're gonna get on with it."

Koosman's MLB career featured the Mets (1967-78), Minnesota Twins (1978-81), Chicago White Sox (1981-83) and Philadelphia Phillies (1983-84).

He was a two-time All-Star (1968-69) and key member of the Mets' 1969 World Series team alongside ace Tom Seaver .

"Jerry was so underrated because Seaver was there, too," Duffy Dyer , the former Mets catcher and Koosman's teammate from 1968-71, told SNY's Anthony McCarron in August 2021.

"His fastball had really good movement and he threw hard. I always thought he was tougher to catch because you didn't know how his fastball was going to move each time -- cut, sink or rise. It was such a great pitch."

Koosman was on SNY's Mets All-Time Team earlier this year.

"Seaver's wingman, Koosman -- whose No. 36 was retired in 2021 -- was a force in his own right during the 12 years he spent with the Mets from 1967 to 1978 -- posting a 3.09 ERA and 1.22 WHIP in over 2,500 innings," SNY's Danny Abriano wrote March 20.

"His most dominant stretch came from 1968 to 1971, and included tossing a complete game in Game 5 of the 1969 World Series as the Mets won their first title."

Koosman was born Dec. 23, 1942, in Appleton, Minn. He made his MLB debut April 14, 1967, with the Mets and last appeared in the bigs as a member of the Phillies Aug. 21, 1985.

articles.title: How Oklahoma State football's widespread defensive faults cost Cowboys vs Iowa State
articles.summary: The 51 points Oklahoma State football’s defense allowed Saturday vs Iowa State are the most the Cowboys have allowed in a game this season.
articles.body:
AMES, IA — Oklahoma State linebacker Ethan Wesloski's answers were short.

He didn't have much to say about his defense's performance in a 51-49 loss at Iowa State.

"I didn't play good enough, didn't play to the standard, simple," Wesloski said.

The 51 points OSU's defense allowed Saturday are the most the Cowboys have allowed in a game this season. Those points sting worse because of the 49 points quarterback Drew Mestemaker and the offense scored.

"It hurts, especially when you know Drew and them are rolling," defensive end James Williams said.

Oklahoma State Cowboys vs Iowa State Cyclones in Week 9 college football game, see photos

Seven touchdowns, a seventh-consecutive 300-yard passing game from Mestemaker, 275 total yards from running back Caleb Hawkins and a go-ahead touchdown pitch to receiver Wyatt Young with 53 seconds remaining couldn't overcome OSU's defensive problems.

Saturday's scene in Ames isn't new. Williams said it felt just like the Colorado game, where seemingly every Cowboy touchdown was answered by the defense giving up a score.

For the fifth consecutive game, OSU trailed at halftime. Just like in a 35-32 loss to Houston, it felt like whichever defense was on the field last would be the loser and OSU's defense couldn't get rid of the hot potato.

With 53 seconds left, Iowa State quarterback Jaylen Raynor connected on a 33-yard pass down the sideline to freshman receiver Jamal Polite Jr. to get Cyclones into field goal territory. It was the seventh Iowa State play that went for 25 or more yards.

Cyclone running back Aiden Flora ran for runs of 4, 3 and 7 yards on his way to a 221-yard day to set up kicker Kyle Konrardy's walk-off 34-yard field goal.

Failures on multiple levels led to OSU allowing 581 yards to Iowa State. That's the most yardage Iowa State's offense has tallied in a Big 12 game since 2016, when the Cyclones went for 608 against Texas.

Just last week, the Cyclones scored three points against Arizona and finished with 221 total yards. That game, a tight end led Iowa State with 42 receiving yards and Raynor was benched at halftime.

There were factors against OSU's defense. The team's leading tackler, linebacker Tate Romney, exited in the third quarter with a hamstring injury. Defensive end Jaleel Johnson appeared on the sideline in the second half with his arm in a sling.

The slick grass in Jack Trice Stadium favored both offenses. because ballcarriers knew where they were going.

Ask around the locker room, and those challenges aren't the reason OSU's defense struggled so much Saturday.

Players believe the defensive shortcomings are because they aren't executing.

"(The Cyclones) did some good stuff, but there wasn't nothing that blew our minds," Wesloski said. "We simply just had to execute and it starts with me."

Coach Eric Morris puts some blame on his staff.

"The most disappointing thing is defensively what they were able to do at will against us," Morris said. "Obviously, they were super balanced, we didn't make them one dimensional at all, they had a ton of explosive runs, explosive passes … that falls on me as the head coach and I'll get that fixed."

Saturday, defensive breakdowns happened because there was slow communication getting the defensive call in from the sideline making the corresponding adjustment on the field.

On multiple third-and-1s, Raynor found a gaping hole in a three-man Cowboy defensive front with quarterback sneak plays. Raynor finished with 48 rushing yards, his most in a Big 12 game this year.

In the third quarter, Cowboy cornerback Mo Horn looked to the sideline for a play call. As his attention remained on the sideline, Iowa State snapped the ball and Polite Jr. ran right by him for a 53-yard reception.

"They ran a lot of 12, 13 personnel, sometimes 14, 21 two-back sets so (defensive coordinator Skyler Cassity) is trying to get us lined up … on that long pass that Mo (gave up) that's exactly what happened," Williams said.

OSU has fallen to No. 14 in the Big 12 in total defense, allowing 391.1 yards per game.

Morris said he'd have to evaluate the film and see how correctable the defensive shortcomings are.

"I trust these guys, what we have," Morris said. "I know our players. Our players are the same that we had all year…and we got to look at it. Are we putting them in the best position? We got to look at ourselves in the mirror as coaches and see if they can handle what we're asking them to do, because this is the first game I felt like pretty much for the whole game we didn't have many answers."

articles.title: Pat Freiermuth Reaches Significant Steelers Milestone
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth has surpassed Bennie Cunningham (2,879) to become the Steelers’ second-leading tight end in career […]
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth has surpassed Bennie Cunningham (2,879) to become the Steelers' second-leading tight end in career receiving yards. Only Steelers legend Heath Miller (6,569) has more receiving yards among tight ends in franchise history.

Freiermuth moved into second place with a 7-yard reception late in the first quarter.

Last year, Freiermuth recorded a career low in offensive snap percentage (51%), targets per game (3.2) and receiving yards per game (2.4), yet he had his most efficient season when it came to yards per target (9) and yards per catch (11).

Things have changed now under Mike McCarthy . Freiermuth is off to a hot start, catching 24 passes for 2007 yards and four touchdowns.

Freiermuth feels like he's being properly utilized.

"I definitely see myself as more of a focal point of the offense," Freiermuth said in early October on The Pat McAfee Show . "Probably in OTAs and camp, I started getting the feel that Aaron [Rodgers] and Coach McCarthy were going to use me and my strengths. And I felt like it was just kind of a natural process, trying to lean on the tight end room with me and Darnell [Washington] throughout the camp and OTAs.

Freiermuth had a standout performance in the Steelers ' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, catching seven passes for 44 yards and two touchdowns.

"I think Coach McCarthy has done a great job of challenging the offense to go out and win games on offense instead of kind of relying on the defense to win those games for us," Freiermuth said. "I feel like we're playing some good complementary team football right now and we just gotta continue to keep going."

Freiermuth also praised McCarthy for being very detailed.

"I thought he was going to be extremely detailed, and he definitely is that," Freiermuth said. "Our schedules are very detailed, very oriented. We're in there throughout the day, really going through meetings throughout the whole day and very structured, which is good. I think the guys have been responsive to it."

articles.title: Arizona and UCLA open in Las Vegas with a rivalry that needs no warmup
articles.summary: Arizona and UCLA do not need a conference game to make their first meeting of the season feel important. A neutral-court opener gives two ranked programs an...
articles.body:
The season is only beginning, but Arizona and UCLA will already share a stage that feels bigger than an ordinary opener. The teams meet Monday at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, where a neutral court puts the focus on the rivalry and the opportunity to begin the year with a statement.

Preseason rankings add another layer to the rivalry

Arizona is ranked No. 5 in the preseason AP poll, while UCLA enters at No. 22. Those numbers make the Wildcats the higher-ranked team, but they also raise the stakes for both sides. Arizona will want to show that its ranking is supported by more than preseason optimism. UCLA can immediately make its own case by challenging a top-five opponent in a high-profile setting.

The game also arrives with the familiarity of a regional rivalry. Arizona and UCLA have spent decades crossing paths as major West Coast programs, and their meetings carry a different energy from an opener against an unfamiliar opponent. The neutral venue removes home-court advantage, leaving both teams to solve the game through execution and composure.

Las Vegas gives both teams a neutral-court test

That matters early in the season, when rotations and roles may still be settling. A team that handles the first wave of pressure, limits mistakes and responds after an opponent's run can gain more than a win. It can gain confidence before the schedule becomes more demanding.

The matchup is part of the Hall of Fame Series ' opening-night slate in Las Vegas, alongside Gonzaga-Purdue. That gives fans a double dose of ranked basketball, but Arizona-UCLA has its own identity: a rivalry meeting placed at the front of the calendar.

For UCLA, the chance is to upset a top-five opponent before the season's rhythm is established. For Arizona, it is a chance to start the year by protecting its status and reminding the sport that the Wildcats expect to be part of the national conversation.

articles.title: Packers defense has already passed 2025 team in this important category
articles.summary: The Packers defense has forced 15 takeaways in eight games, already beating last season's total.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers needed only eight games in 2026 to top last season's takeaway total. Jonathan Gannon's defense created two more takeaways during Thursday night's win over the Carolina Panthers , pushing the team's total to 15 -- which leads the NFL (entering Sunday) and is already one more than last season's total of 14.

The Packers have created multiple takeaways in five straight games. Green Bay is 4-1 in those games, reviving the season after a 1-2 start.

Last season, the Packers produced only seven interceptions in 17 games. Through eight games in 2026, the Packers have an NFL-high 10 interceptions.

Gannon's scheme is aggressive, and he's been unafraid to blitz, so it comes as no surprise that pressure is helping create turnovers. Per Next Gen Stats, pressure has helped caused six of the 15 takeaways, and Devonte Wyatt and Lukas Van Ness have both created a pair of turnovers off pressure.

Takeaways are incredibly important to wins and losses but also incredibly volatile year over year. In 2024, Jeff Hafley's first-year Packers defense produced 31 takeaways. A year later, and after adding Micah Parsons, the total dropped to only 14. Now, Gannon's Packers defense is on pace for 32 takeaways through eight games.

Can the Packers continue to take the football away?

articles.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown injury update as Lions WR returns to game against Vikings
articles.summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown left the Lions' game against the Vikings on Sunday but then returned in the second quarter after being evaluated.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown left Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter but returned on the ensuing series.

St. Brown appeared to come down hard while attempting to haul in a would-be touchdown pass from Jared Goff in the back of the end zone.

The 24-yard connection was initially ruled a completion, but the ruling was reversed upon review.

St. Brown went to the locker room to be evaluated as the offense returned to the field.

He returned on the ensuing series with a wrap on his left knee.

articles.title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson ruled out after hurting thumb on right throwing hand
articles.summary: (AP) — Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out after hurting the thumb on his right throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive snap against the...
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out after hurting the thumb on his right throwing hand on Baltimore's first offensive snap against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

Jackson was hurt in his first start after missing three games with an ankle injury, and while dropping back and bouncing a pass attempt to Zay Flowers. Jackson was unable to finish his follow-through as his right hand struck pass rusher Greg Rousseau's arm.

Jackson immediately began heading off the field and appeared to point to his thumb before taking a knee before reaching the sideline. He was immediately escorted up the tunnel with backup Tyler Huntley taking over.

After initially listing Jackson as questionable, the Ravens listed him as out before the first quarter ended.

Baltimore (4-3) went 1-2 in Jackson's absence in a stretch in which the Ravens offensive production drastically dropped off under Huntley. Baltimore scored 63 fewer points and averaged 3 fewer yards per play in the past three games as opposed to the first three under Jackson.

articles.title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson with right thumb injury
articles.summary: Tyler Huntley has replcaed Jackson.
articles.body:
The Ravens have ruled out Lamar Jackson. The question is: How bad is his right thumb injury?

Jackson started for the first time since Oct. 4, missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain, but he lasted one play against the Bills.

The Ravens quarterback got hit on an incompletion intended for Zay Flowers and immediately left the field. The team's medical staff took him to the X-ray room.

Tyler Huntley, who was 1-2 in Jackson's absence, replaced him. He is 2-for-3 for no yards.

The Bills lead 10-7 after a Josh Allen pass intended for tight end Jackson Hawes was batted into the air by Hawes and defensive lineman Broderick Washington intercepted it at the Buffalo 17. The Ravens scored on Derrick Henry's 2-yard run.

Henry is only the third player in NFL history to record 40 or more rushing touchdowns with two different franchises.

articles.title: Raiders’ Ashton Jeanty eviscerated by Rex Ryan for calling out Jets players as soft
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are currently preparing to hit the field to take on the lowly New York Jets on Sunday afternoon on the road. Raiders running back Ashto...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are currently preparing to hit the field to take on the lowly New York Jets on Sunday afternoon on the road. Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty made headlines this week when he called out the Jets' players for not wanting to tackle ahead of the matchup, setting the stage for what could be some bad blood on the field on Sunday.

One person not on board with those comments is former Jets head coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan .

"Is this kid a joke or what? Does he not look at the tape? Because when I look at the tape, I see that. I see DeMario Davis not losing a step, still playing at the top of his game. But you know what else I see? How about Mr. Tiptoe through the Tulips, avoiding contact? This guy's soft as Charmin," he said, per Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While Ryan has become known for making hyperbolic takes during his time at ESPN, it will still be a sentiment appreciated by Jets fans ahead of the matchup.

Making Jeanty's comments all the more puzzling is the fact that he has not exactly had a great first half of the season so far, struggling to put up meaningful production as the Raiders have come crashing back to Earth after their hot start, now having lost four straight games.

Jeanty may have also provided the Jets' defense with some unnecessary bulletin board material ahead of the game.

In any case, the Raiders and Jets are slated to get things kicked off on Sunday at 1:00 pm ET from the Meadowlands.
