articles.title: Jared Verse gets dumped by Mason McCormick on extra-point try
articles.summary: If Browns defensive end Jared Verse is going to whine about the Steelers being dirty, the Steelers are apparently going to give him something to whine about.
articles.body:
If Browns defensive end Jared Verse is going to whine about the Steelers being dirty, the Steelers are apparently going to give him something to whine about.

On the extra-point try after Pittsburgh's first touchdown of the game, Steelers guard Mason McCormick lifted Verse off the ground and dumped him on his head , Joe "Turkey" Jones-style .

Verse took McCormick's helmet with him as he made his journey from the air to the land.

McCormick was penalized on the play, and he'll likely be fined. But it sends an early message to a player who dared to poke the black-and-gold bear.

articles.title: Lakers vs. Raptors: Three things to watch as L.A. looks to bounce back
articles.summary: The Lakers return home for Game 7, looking to clean up their turnovers, get more from their reserves and slow down Scottie Barnes.
articles.body:
The Lakers showed how quickly their offense can build a lead Friday. They also showed how quickly that advantage can disappear.

After surrendering a 25-point lead in a 112-95 loss to the Warriors, the Lakers (4-2) return to Crypto.com Arena to face the Toronto Raptors (3-2) on Sunday. Their seventh game presents another opportunity to address the uneven execution that has contributed to two losses in the last three games.

The Lakers committed 20 turnovers against Golden State, with Austin Reaves responsible for eight. Luka Dončić's 37 points helped fuel their offense, but L.A. struggled to sustain possessions as the Warriors recovered from their early deficit.

Toronto presents another challenge for the Lakers' ballhandlers. The Raptors are averaging 12.4 steals, which ranks second in the NBA through five games.

The Lakers have already demonstrated their scoring ability. Turning more possessions into shot attempts would give that offense a better chance to hold up across four quarters.

Golden State's bench outscored the Lakers' reserves 50-7 on Friday, a significant disparity in a game L.A. lost by 17.

That followed a win over the Clippers in which the Lakers received important contributions throughout the rotation without Dončić. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton have shown they can bring scoring and defensive activity, but the Lakers need those contributions alongside their leading scorer, too, and at a consistent level.

Watch how JJ Redick distributes the ballhandling responsibilities when he begins making substitutions.

Barnes enters Sunday after scoring a career-high 41 points in Toronto's 121-114 loss to Orlando. He has led the Raptors in scoring in four of their first five games.

His size and ability to operate inside present a different defensive assignment from chasing Golden State's shooters.

The Lakers must make Barnes work for positioning while keeping their help organized behind the initial defender. Allowing him to establish himself deep in the paint would put additional pressure on Walker Kessler to protect the rim.

How L.A. handles those possessions without surrendering open looks elsewhere will be central to its response. After losing control of Friday's game, the Lakers need a more connected defensive effort to finish their first meeting with Toronto.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson ruled out with thumb injury after one pass
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left the Week 8 game due to a thumb injury in the first quarter, and he was ruled out.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (thumb) was able to return from an ankle injury to start Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills , but he hit his right thumb on a helmet on a pass attempt follow through, and he was quickly ruled out.

He attempted just a single pass, which ended up incomplete, before heading for the blue medical tent. It's possible that he suffered a broken thumb, but that hasn't yet been verified. However, he was ruled out very quickly, which in indicative of a more serious injury.

Why it Matters: It's a bummer for fantasy managers, as Jackson just missed several games due to an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley took back over, and he'll likely be the starter in Week 9 on a short week, as the Ravens play again on Thursday night, although that is not yet confirmed.

Running back Bhayshul Tuten also came out briefly with an injury but missed only one offensive series. He gained 28 yards on six carries on the Jaguars' opening TD reception.

articles.title: Cowboys Seek Rare Win Streak As Healthy Defense Faces Arizona
articles.summary: Dallas looks for back-to-back wins against Arizona. Brian Schottenheimer discusses the defense's health and the need for consistency. Read the latest.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys finally have a spark after a big win on the road. They crushed the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 last Monday night. Now the team must prove it can do it again on Sunday. Brian Schottenheimer knows the job is not done yet. He needs his squad to stay consistent to keep rolling.

Dallas sits at 3-4 on the season. This week brings a visit from the Arizona Cardinals. The Cowboys have not won back-to-back games in nearly a year and a half. That streak ended a long time ago. Schottenheimer said the team must fix their execution issues to stay alive in the race.

The offense found a new gear against Philadelphia. They ran for 204 total yards in that game. Javonte Williams led the way with 155 yards on the ground. That was a career high for him. Prior to this contest, the Cowboys possessed the NFL's second-least productive rushing attack. They used traps and misdirection to create huge gains. Blogging The Boys noted the team finally showed a real commitment to the run.

The Cardinals defense is no pushover though. They rank sixth in the league for stopping the run. Dallas must keep their running game alive if they want to win. The offense cannot just sit back and hope for big plays in the air. They need to control the clock and keep Arizona off the field.

The defense has been a mess for most of the season. Entering Week 8, Dallas holds the bottom ranking for run defense. They also sit 24th in points allowed per game. But things look different now. DeMarvion Overshown is back on the field. His return changes the entire feel of the unit.

Schottenheimer told 105.3 The Fan he was happy to see the linebacker return. "You felt (DeMarvion Overshown) coming back, I thought that was great," Schotty said. The coach believes health is the key to their success. "I think getting healthy is a big part of it," he added. "Overall, I think the health of this defense is what's getting us really excited," he added. "We're getting bodies back and that's huge for us."

Even with these improvements, the numbers are scary. Dallas ranks 20th in pass defense. They allowed 21 points to Philadelphia, which was their second-fewest this season. But the Eagles were missing their star quarterback Jalen Hurts and two top receivers. Saquon Barkley was also not fully healthy. The Cowboys cannot rely on a lucky break against Arizona.

The Cardinals have a strange history with Dallas. They have won nine of the last 10 meetings. Arizona is perfect in four visits to AT&T Stadium. They are 2-2 on the road this year. The Cardinals just broke a four-game losing streak by beating the Los Angeles Rams. They are dangerous and ready to strike.

Schottenheimer knows the danger of this opponent. He warned his team about the challenges ahead. "It's a business where you have to be consistent with your execution, with your performance," he said. "And I think we've been lacking that at times." The coach wants his players to focus on the week at hand. "Where I always try to put my focus is that this is a week-to-week league," said Arizona coach Mike LaFleur.

Dallas has four home games in the next five weeks.

articles.title: Former Phillies Starter, Rival’s 2-Time All-Star And World Series Champion Jerry Koosman, Dies
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies received news that a former star trade acquisition who joined a division rival’s Hall of Fame has died.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies have been part of some of baseball's most memorable eras, and their long history includes tenures from many of the most notable players in major league history, whose careers extended well beyond their time in Philadelphia.

One former standout Phillies starter joined the team after a career that was defined by the New York Mets, where he became one of the key figures of the franchise's early success. He eventually finished his career with the Phillies, offering fans of the franchise a chance to call him one of their own as well.

And after a memorable 19 year career in the big leagues, the Mets shared the news that he died at age 83 on Sunday.

Former Philadelphia Phillies Starter, World Series Champion Dies After Battling Multiple Illnesses

"The 1969 Mets had a multitude of heroes, but no one was bigger than Jerry Koosman, who passed away this morning after battling multiple illnesses," longtime Mets public relations representative Jay Horwitz announced .

The Mets confirmed his death in a remembrance published on their official blog, which also shared details about his family and his place in franchise history.

"Jerry who was 83 years old died in Osceola, WI surrounded by his family," according to the memorial post . "His number 36 is retired by the New York Mets and he is also in the team's Hall of Fame. After the Mets lost game 1 of the World Series, Jerry won game 2 and also the clinching game 5 ."

Koosman spent 12 seasons with the Mets from 1967 through 1978, forming a formidable pitching tandem with Tom Seaver. He was a two-time All-Star, earning selections in 1968 and 1969, and played a major role in New York's improbable 1969 World Series championship.

But longtime Phillies fans will recall that he spent the final two campaigns of his career, 1984 and 1985, with their favorite team after his impressive run with arguably their fiercest division rival.

Philadelphia Phillies, New York Mets Star Dies After Championship Career

After leaving New York, Koosman pitched for the Minnesota Twins and Chicago White Sox before joining the Phillies. All told, his 19-year career ended with 222 wins, 2,556 strikeouts and a 3.36 ERA over 612 appearances

Though his time with the Phillies represented just the closing chapter of a long playing career, Koosman's legacy will be treasured in Philadelphia. His role in the Mets' rise from perennial underdogs to World Series champions made him one of the most recognizable pitchers in that franchise's history, making his arrival with the Phillies quite notable at the time.

Koosman made 18 starts in his final season with the Phillies, logging a 4.62 ERA, before hanging up his spikes.

articles.title: Raiders give all 1st quarter carries to Mike Washington over Ashton Jeanty
articles.summary: Mike Washington got all the carriees to start Raiders Week 8 vs Jets following Ashton Jeanty's controversial comments this week.
articles.body:
There was quite an interesting situation with Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders ' Week 8 matchup with the Jets. Despite being named a captain for the game, the Raider took the ball out of his hands for the entire first quarter, giving all the carries to rookie Mike Washington.

It's interesting not just because Jeanty was named a captain, but because it comes on the heels of J eanty's comment from the Raiders locker room mocking the Jets' defenders , saying that some of them don't like to tackle.

The statement sparked a strong reaction from the Jets players and became a national story. This included Jets LB Demario Davis who called it "bulletin board material."

Honestly, it could be punishment for Jeanty's comments or his ineffectiveness running the ball that caused the Raiders to make the switch. Jeanty has averaged just 3.1 yards per carry this season while Washington has put up 4.9 yards per carry.

Washington had six carries for 21 yards (3.5 ypc) on two possessions for the Raiders to open this game. Jeanty came out and lined up out wide, but has yet to touch the ball.

articles.title: Skubal’s Record Deal Could Break White Sox Free Agency
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal's potential $355 million contract looms over the White Sox offseason. Can the South Side spend big on Freddy Peralta while the market shifts?
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox have a narrow window to fix their pitching, but the market is shifting beneath their feet. Tarik Skubal is likely to shatter every record for a pitcher with a deal worth eight years and $355 million, according to ESPN . That number is the average of 27 projections from insiders polled by Kiley McDaniel. It is a massive sum that could drain the payroll for years to come. The 2026-27 free agent class is considered one of the weakest in a decade. They need help, but the top tier of the market is priced out of reach.

Skubal will be 30 in 2027 and posted a 2.72 ERA with 186 strikeouts this season. His stats are elite, yet his medical history raises red flags for a long-term commitment. He had Tommy John surgery in college and elbow surgery in 2022. He even underwent a procedure in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow. That minimally invasive surgery allowed him to pitch at a Cy Young level for the rest of the season. The White Sox cannot ignore this risk. The team paid a record price for an arm with three past surgeries.

Chasing Skubal might be a mistake when better value exists elsewhere. The White Sox need starting pitchers and position players more than anything else, says Yahoo Sports . While the market has more starting pitching talent than outfielders, the best position players like Randy Arozarena are still available. Pursuing Freddy Peralta makes more sense than betting the farm on Skubal. Yahoo Sports notes that going after Peralta or Michael King while also targeting top position players is a tall order. The team has six players entering free agency, including pitchers Erick Fedde and Sean Newcomb, per Sports Mockery . Newcomb threw 90.1 innings with a 3.09 ERA last season, per Sports Mockery. The Sox must find a way to fill holes without breaking the bank on one risky arm.

The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec 1. They have to weigh the cost of a $355 million contract against the need for immediate depth. If they overspend on Skubal, they might lose out on the position players they also need.

articles.title: Notre Dame beats Villanova 74-72 in men’s college basketball season opener in Rome
articles.summary: Brady Koehler scored key baskets down the stretch and Notre Dame made a late comeback after trailing for most of the second half to beat Villanova 74-72 in the college basketball season opener in Rome on Sunday.
articles.body: ROME — Brady Koehler scored key baskets down the stretch and Notre Dame made a late comeback after trailing for most of the second half to beat Villanova 74-72 in the college basketball season opener in Rome on Sunday. Villanova standout Tyler Perkins fouled out with 16.3 seconds to go. He led the Wildcats with 18 points. The event — dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off — included an audience with Villanova alumnus Pope Leo XIV for both teams and their fans on Saturday. Both teams are unranked in the preseason AP Top 25. Koehler and Braeden Smith led Notre Dame, which has 10 new players, with 16 points each. Koehler’s dunk cut Villanova’s lead to one point with 1:36 remaining and Logan Duncomb hit a 3-pointer with 1:08 to go to give Notre Dame its first lead of the second half, 70-68. Koehler sank two free throws to put the Fighting Irish up 74-70 with 4 seconds remaining and essentially seal it. Villanova is looking for a revival after four years without winning a game at the NCAA Tournament: A three-year absence followed the sudden retirement of Hall of Fame coach Jay Wright and then the Wildcats had a first-round loss to Utah State last season. Luigi Suigo, the 7-foot-3 Italian making his Villanova debut on home soil, had two dunks and showed his range with a 3-pointer to finish with seven points. When he scored, the arena announcer yelled, “Su-su-su Suigo.” The nonconference game between the two Catholic universities was played at the 11,000-seat Palazzo dello Sport, which is located about a half-hour drive from the Vatican. Villanova had many more fans in attendance. It’s a doubleheader and a women’s game between the two schools was up next. Up next Notre Dame faces another Catholic school in its home opener against Mercyhurst on Thursday. Villanova faces two more Catholic schools in its next two games: The Wildcats play Holy Cross in their home opener on Friday and then meet La Salle four days later.
